problem: Existing MARL cooperative-exploration methods assume fully synchronous decision making with atomic, instantaneous actions, but real robots take varying wall-clock times per action or drop offline. Waiting for the slowest robot wastes time and blocks the whole team.
motivation: Real-time exploration efficiency is measured in wall-clock time, not in action-making steps, so a synchronous formulation mismatches real deployment. Policies should be trained asynchronously, be robust to action delays, tolerate robots being lost, and communicate cheaply.
key_idea: Train a team-size-invariant multi-tower CNN+attention policy with an asynchronous MAPPO (Async-MAPPO, bi-level macro actions, per-agent caches) plus action-delay randomization, so robots replan whenever they finish and exchange only low-dimensional CNN features.
insight: Matching training to asynchronous execution helps: ACE, trained with asynchronous data and delay randomization, beats synchronous-trained MAPPO in real-time Time (real robot 25.61 s vs 28.48 s). Delay randomization needs a moderate interval: 3-5 gives 48.88 Time in the 4⇒3 lost-agent case, while 1-10 gives 60.24. Learned CNN features are an efficient message: ACE with 4-channel features matches or slightly exceeds sharing the merged raw observation (Perf. Comm.), and No Comm. is far worse (159.26 vs 74.36).
method: Async-MAPPO: MAPPO adapted to the Dec-POSMDP setting; rewards are accumulated between macro-action steps, and each agent stores transitions in its own cache that is pushed to a central buffer, so no synchronized environment steps are needed.

Action-delay randomization: after each macro action, force the agent to wait a random 3-5 execution steps (grid) or 10-15 (Habitat) to simulate execution time and failures for sim-to-real generalization.

Multi-tower CNN Policy (MCP): a weight-sharing 3-layer CNN maps each agent's SxSx7 local map (obstacle, explored, location, trajectory, 3 view channels) to a GxGx4 feature; agents exchange only these features, cutting traffic by ~93-97%.
Relation encoder: a simplified Transformer block with multi-head cross-attention fuses the agents' feature maps into one team-size-invariant representation, so it handles agent loss.

Action decoder: a categorical distribution over grid cells gives the global goal; in Habitat it adds two continuous point heads for a relative offset inside an 8x8 region cell (hierarchical to handle multimodality). A* / local policy executes atomic actions.
Reward: team coverage reward, an individual coverage reward (Habitat), a success reward at C% coverage (98 grid / 90 Habitat), and an overlap penalty active while coverage < 0.9.
Real deployment: Mecanum robots on Jetson Nano with OptiTrack localization; each robot requests the latest peer features over ROS when it finishes its actions.

setting.backbone: Multi-tower CNN + transformer-attention policy (trained from scratch with Async-MAPPO); Habitat also uses pretrained Neural SLAM and local policy
setting.training_data: RL in simulation only: 50M steps in grid simulator, 100M steps in Habitat (Gibson maps), 3 seeds; no extra data
setting.observation: Top-down local 2D maps (obstacle, explored, location, trajectory, agent-view channels) from mapping / Neural SLAM; RGB in Habitat via SLAM
setting.action_space: Bi-level: global goal (grid cell / continuous point) as macro action, then atomic forward / turn left / turn right
setting.privileged: none for ACE (OptiTrack used for localization in real world); planning baselines use global information

numbers_note: Exploration coverage-time task; none of the listed canonical navigation benchmarks apply (custom grid simulator, Habitat/Gibson multi-agent exploration, and a real-robot test), so no benchmark rows are reported.
results: In the 2-agent grid simulator ACE has the lowest exploration Time, e.g. 18.66 vs 21.92 (MAPPO) on 15x15 asynchronous and 74.36 vs 82.55 on 25x25. In the real world ACE needs 25.61 s vs 28.48 s (MAPPO, -10.07%) and 38.72 s (Nearest, -33.86%). In Habitat ACE gets 127.62 Time vs 133.23 (MAPPO) and >=28% less than planners, and it generalizes to agent loss.
limitations: Communication errors, localization errors and sensor noise are not handled (OptiTrack localization in real world); real tests are only 2 robots on a 15x15 grid map.
Habitat ACE has higher Overlap than some planning baselines, and simulation Time is estimated from a fixed time model rather than measured.
Each robot's policy depends on peers' features, but delay randomization intervals need manual tuning.
builds_on: Learning Efficient Multi-Agent Cooperative Visual Exploration
